newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU freezes ties with Iran but sends envoys back.
newsitem.headline: EU freezes ties with Iran but sends envoys back.

text.p: The European Union on Tuesday suspended ministerial ties with Iran in a firm response to a recent German court ruling that cited Iran's rulers for ordering political assassinations.
The move was seen as a political gesture reflecting the EU's determination to fight international terrorism.

"This is a substantial and muscular response to the Mykonos case," said European Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan, referring to the 1992 slayings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant.
Three weeks ago, EU governments recalled their envoys from the Iranian capital after a Berlin court accused Tehran of ordering the murder of the four Kurds.
Tehran has denied involvement in the German murders and earlier this month expelled four German diplomats from Tehran in a tit-for-tat response to Bonn kicking out four Iranian envoys.
EU foreign ministers meeting in Luxembourg agreed that ambassadors could now return to Tehran if individual countries wanted them to.
"There was consensus that the ambassadors could go back...from today," German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said.

The EU said in a statement that it would continue its arms embargo on Iran, refuse visas to Iranians with intelligence or security functions and move to exclude all Iranian intelligence personnel from Europe.
"Under the present circumstances...there is no basis for the continuation of the critical dialogue between the EU and Iran," it said.
An EU diplomat said that the suspension of high-level contact with Tehran proved the 15-nation bloc could deliver a coordinated follow-up to the withdrawal of its ambassadors.
"This is confirmation of the EU's condemnation of state inspired acts of terrorism," he said.
Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, speaking for the EU presidency, said he was satisfied that ministers had sent Tehran a tough message.
"I think Europe has shown a common position of value and I'm happy with that," he told reporters.
The National Council of Resistance of Iran, which opposes the Tehran government, also welcomed the EU stance.

"This...shows that the conscience of the European Union is awakening to the issue of Iranian terrorism. This was a necessary reaction," a spokesman said, adding that the EU should now sever all ties with Iran, impose a trade embargo and end the critical dialogue for good.
The EU's policy of critical dialogue has involved talking to Tehran while trying to get Iran to move closer to the West.
The return of EU ambassadors is seen as a sign that the EU is reluctant to damage its lucrative ties with Iran. The bloc is Iran's biggest trading partner.
But the suspension of ministerial ties could hamper plans by several EU member states to send trade delegations to Tehran on the back of ministerial visits, one senior EU official said.
EU officials said that the bloc would now require unanimity to resurrect the critical dialogue with Iran. "This is the death-knell for the criticial dialogue policy," one said.

The United States has urged the EU to take a hard line against Tehran and join economic sanctions Washington has imposed on Iran for alleged sponsorship of international terrorism. Iran denies the charges.
The ambassadors' return should also help missions monitor Iranian presidential elections on May 23 when President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani steps down after eight years, diplomats said.
